findings.note: ESPN's Game 2 page lists Freddy Peralta for the Rays (1.93 postseason ERA, 0.86 WHIP) against Parker Messick for Cleveland (5.40 ERA, 6 walks in 6.2 IP). The 98-64 Rays went 55-26 at home and are favored, though starter Shane McClanahan is listed out and Cleveland trails Game 1 1-0.

CBS says Cleveland beat the Rays 7-3 in Game 1 for a four-game winning streak. Cleveland scored seven runs in the last four innings off a Rays staff that had allowed five runs in a three-game sweep of the Yankees, while the Rays' hits were almost all singles.

MLB.com says Cleveland used starter Foster Griffin for four innings and then five relievers plus closer Cade Smith in Game 1, after a five-game ALDS. That bullpen workload could matter in Game 2, but Cleveland's relievers held the Rays down.

Game 2 of the ALCS is at Tropicana Field, Parker Messick (5.40 ERA, 1.80 WHIP, 6 walks in 6.2 postseason innings) against Freddy Peralta (1.93 ERA). ESPN's listed total is 7, so the 6.5 line on this bet is half a run lower than that market.

Cleveland beat Tampa Bay 7-3 in Game 1, a 10-run game. Starter Foster Griffin lasted only four innings and was followed by five relievers going one inning each, so Cleveland's bullpen could be tired for Game 2.
Says the Rays staff allowed only 5 runs in 27 innings against the Yankees before giving up 7 runs in four innings in Game 1. It also says Cleveland wore out its pitching staff in a five-game ALDS.

MLB.com confirms Peralta starts ALCS Game 2. It says he had a 0.96 ERA over 28 innings in five September starts, about 17 outs per start, and quotes Kevin Cash saying he has found ways to get deep in games.

In his only start this postseason, the Rays pulled Peralta after 4 2/3 innings (14 outs) while he was holding the Yankees to one run. That is just over the 13.5 line and shows Tampa Bay may pull him early even when he is pitching well.

ESPN reports that before the trade, Peralta failed to finish five innings in 15 of his 22 Mets starts, and his strikeout and whiff rates dropped. That is evidence for short outings, though it predates his run with the Rays.

MLB.com's Game 1 recap says Caminero avoided serious injury in a late-game collision with outfielder Jonny DeLuca and puts the focus back on him for Tuesday's Game 2, but it gives no practice or lineup confirmation for this game.

CBS's Game 1 live blog shows Caminero hit an RBI single early, then Cleveland relievers struck him out twice (Espino in the 5th, Gaddis on a changeup in the 7th), and he went down clutching his chest after the collision before staying in the game.

A Covers analyst picked Caminero Over 1.5 hits+runs+RBI for Game 1 against lefty Foster Griffin, pointing to his .390 wOBA against left-handers. That pick was for a different game and market, not Game 2 total bases.
